newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Naphtha down, mogas supported.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Naphtha down, mogas supported.

text.p: Naphtha fell with crude amid good supplies but gasoline held steady amid lack of bearish indicators, traders said on Monday
"Naphtha is down but I think gasoline is steady...there is no talk that it is bearish," a trader with a major oil company said.
The gasoline fob Singapore market was silent and offered no direction but traders were balanced to bullish on the outlook, in anticipation of demand emerging from Indonesia for July.
They also said India's purchase was at a good level.

State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) bought by tender 25,000-tonnes of 87-octane leaded gasoline for June 18-22 delivery at $43 per tonne above MidEast naphtha quotes, c+f Bombay on the west coast, a source close to IOC said.

"The price is much better than when IOC bought the last time which was about $15 per tonne higher," the source said on IOC's last purchase by tender of 90,000-tonnes of 87-octane leaded gasoline for March delivery to the west coast.
But traders said the award was equivalent to around Singapore 92-octane unleaded quotes plus $3.50, c+f Bombay or $2.00 fob Singapore.
"That is very good," a trader said.

Adding further support to the market, IOC is seeking a second gasoline cargo - for June 26-30 delivery - to the west coast because of a product shortfall caused by the emergency shutdown of the 150,000 barrel-per-day facility belonging to state refiner Cochin Refineries Ltd.
Production at the refinery, located on the southwest coast of India, stopped on June 5 due to water disruption to the refinery and resumed on Saturday.
The tender closes June 12 and is valid for a day.
Talk on the prompt June naphtha swaps was thin as the market rolled forward.
July swaps weakened to $21.15/$21.20 per barrel, down from Friday's $21.45/$21.60.
August was talked in contango to July, at $21.10/$21.30.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
